meta.subtitle: The shares have halved from their high; on adjusted earnings they look cheap, but leverage after the Eddyfi deal and Middle East disruption are real risks

analystCommentary:
ESAB's share price has fallen hard. At $69.90 on October 2, 2026 the stock sits near its 52-week low of $64.83 and about half its high of $137.42. The data we hold does not say what drove the decline, and we have no news coverage that explains it.

The filing shows two plausible pressures. ESAB closed its acquisition of Eddyfi on June 1, 2026, for consideration of approximately $1.5 billion, which lifted leverage. And the MD&A says the Middle East conflict, including the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, reduced sales levels and raised inventory costs in the six months ended July 3, 2026.

Against that, the business is still growing, the Street remains positive, and the shares now trade at a low multiple of consensus earnings (see Valuation). We think the price discounts more damage than the filing shows, but the leverage and the unexplained decline keep our target well below the Street's.

We rate ESAB BUY with a $75–$95 target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
ESAB Corporation formulates, develops, manufactures and supplies consumable products and equipment for cutting, joining and automated welding, as well as gas control equipment. It sells through independent distributors and direct salespeople to a highly diversified industrial customer base.

The company describes itself as a focused premier industrial compounder, run under its ESAB Business Excellence system, EBXai. In June 2026 it added Eddyfi, an advanced inspection and monitoring technology business headquartered in Québec, Canada.

ESAB was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in North Bethesda, Maryland. The 10-K says approximately 80% of its 2025 sales came from operations outside the United States.

thesis.body: The market is pricing ESAB as if its earnings power were impaired. The filing shows a business that is still growing, with consensus expecting higher earnings in FY26E and FY27E, now with a new inspection business added. If ESAB delivers anything close to consensus and starts paying down debt, the shares should recover part of the decline. The scenario math in Valuation supports a BUY, with a target well below the Street's to reflect leverage and the unknown cause of the sell-off.

catalysts: Integration of Eddyfi and its contribution to results.
Easing of Middle East logistics disruption.
Any recovery of IEEPA tariff refunds, which ESAB has not yet recorded as receivables.
risks: High leverage after the Eddyfi acquisition.
Continued Middle East and Ukraine-related disruption.
A cyclical downturn in industrial capital spending.
An unexplained share-price decline that may reflect information not in our data.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $2.8B, up {+3.7%+}, after a {-1.2%-} dip in FY24. Operating margin peaked at 16.3% in FY24 and eased to 14.5% in FY25; diluted EPS was $3.67, down from $4.31.

In the quarter ended July 3, 2026, which our data labels Q3'26, revenue was $807.6M, up 12.9%. That figure includes about one month of Eddyfi. Operating margin for the quarter was 9.7%, well below the FY25 level, and the trailing net margin is 5.7%. The MD&A cites decreased sales levels and higher inventory and raw material costs from the Middle East conflict and tariffs.

The counter-case to our BUY sits here: margins are moving the wrong way at the moment the company has taken on more debt. Some of the margin decline likely reflects acquisition costs, but the excerpt does not break those out, so we cannot separate one-off costs from operating pressure.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt was $1.2B and net debt $1B at the end of FY25, before the Eddyfi acquisition. Trailing net debt to EBITDA is 4.7x, a high level for a cyclical industrial. The trailing current ratio is 1.96.

Part of the acquisition was funded through a February 2026 private placement of 6.50% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock with an aggregate liquidation preference of $175.0 million. The excerpt does not detail the rest of the financing. The preferred will convert into common stock, so holders face some future dilution as well as higher leverage.

The filing also flags asbestos-related liabilities and pension obligations as ongoing exposures, which add to the claims ahead of the common equity.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $213.3M in FY25, a 7.5% FCF margin, down from 11.1% in FY24. Capital expenditure was -$47.3M. The proxy reports free cash flow of $246.1 million for FY25 on the company's own definition; we use the figure from our data, which is lower.

At FY25 levels, free cash flow would take several years to pay down the acquisition debt, so deleveraging will depend on Eddyfi's contribution and on margins recovering. Dividends of -$21.9M in FY25 are small relative to cash flow and do not constrain the balance sheet.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $69.90 ESAB trades at 25.3x trailing earnings, 12.8x NTM earnings, ~10.8x FY27E earnings, 1.4x trailing sales and 14.1x trailing EV/EBITDA.

The gap between trailing and forward multiples is large. Consensus EPS is $5.45 for FY26E and $6.48 for FY27E, well above FY25 diluted EPS. The proxy reports FY25 core adjusted earnings per share of $5.27, so consensus is most likely on that adjusted basis; on GAAP earnings the shares are more expensive than the forward multiple suggests.

The Street is strongly positive: 10 Buy and 1 Hold, with a consensus target of $126.91, a median of $128.00 and a range of $100.00–$145.00. Even the lowest Street target is well above today's price. We set our range far below that because our data does not explain the sell-off.

We have no peer multiples to compare against.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Eddyfi integrates smoothly, Middle East disruption eases, margins recover and debt falls. The market regains confidence and the shares move into the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: ESAB delivers close to consensus adjusted earnings, starts reducing leverage, and the forward multiple recovers part of its decline. The shares rise but stay well below the bottom of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Industrial demand weakens while leverage is high, estimates fall, and the market continues to price ESAB as a stretched, cyclical balance sheet. The shares break below the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it needs only partial delivery against consensus and a partial recovery in the multiple. Bear carries more weight than Bull because leverage is high, margins fell in the latest quarter, and the cause of the decline is unknown. Bull still carries a quarter of the weight because the Street's targets show how far sentiment could recover if execution holds.

The result is a weighted fair value of $80.75, an expected upside of +15.5% and a bear-case downside of -28.5%. The reward/risk clears our BUY threshold, but only modestly, which is why we do not go further.

Our $75–$95 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Our sources disagree on segments. The vendor data carries one consolidated segment, while the 10-Q MD&A says ESAB reports two: the Americas, covering North and South America, and EMEA & APAC, covering Europe, the Middle East, India, Africa and Asia Pacific. We use the filing. Per the 10-K, 40% and 60% of FY25 net sales came from the Americas and EMEA & APAC, respectively. That mix gives ESAB more exposure to Europe and emerging markets, and to the current Middle East disruption, than a U.S.-centered industrial.

moatFactors.name: Consumables and installed base
moatFactors.body: The MD&A describes a business mix balanced between equipment and consumables. Consumables such as welding wire and cutting parts are bought repeatedly by users of installed equipment, which smooths revenue through the cycle.

moatFactors.name: Brand and distribution
moatFactors.body: ESAB has operated since 1904 and sells through independent distributors and direct salespeople worldwide, with principal manufacturing facilities in 16 countries outside the United States. That scale and reach are hard for a small entrant to match.

moatFactors.name: Business system and acquisitions
moatFactors.body: Management says its experience of acquiring and integrating businesses positions it to capture future opportunities, and EBXai is meant to drive continuous improvement. The Eddyfi deal will test that claim at a larger scale than recent acquisitions.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Recurring consumables demand and an established brand protect the core business, and margins held in a mid-teens range through FY25. The 10-K says the welding and cutting industry is mature and cyclical in developed markets, which limits pricing power and growth. Eddyfi moves ESAB into inspection and monitoring, which could widen the moat if it integrates well.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$3.1B, up 8%, and FY27E revenue of $3.4B, helped by the Eddyfi acquisition.
Eddyfi's revenues totaled approximately $240 million for 2025, per the MD&A. A full year of Eddyfi adds meaningfully to the revenue base and moves ESAB toward inspection and monitoring.
Management expects strategic acquisitions to contribute to growth, but with leverage already high, in our view further large deals are unlikely until debt falls.
The MD&A says ESAB has received an insignificant amount of IEEPA tariff refunds so far and has recorded no refund receivables. Any further refunds would be upside not in the current numbers.

management.leadership: Per the proxy statement dated March 2026, Shyam P. Kambeyanda is President and Chief Executive Officer and Kevin J. Johnson is Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The proxy says management recommended that executive officers forgo their cash bonuses for fiscal 2025, given results against expectations, and the Board accepted. That is a sign of accountability. These facts predate the 10-Q and may have changed.
management.capitalAllocation:
The Eddyfi acquisition is the defining capital-allocation decision of 2026. Paying approximately $1.5 billion for a business with 2025 revenues of approximately $240 million is a high price, and it was made with leverage already meaningful. Its success depends on growth and synergies that the filing does not quantify.

ESAB pays a small dividend and the data shows no share repurchases in FY21 to FY25. In our view, cash flow should go to debt reduction until leverage falls, and we would view any new large acquisition in the near term as a negative.
management.governance:
Per the proxy statement dated March 2026, the Board determined that Mr. Rales, Mr. Allender, Ms. Cummings, Ms. Jordan, Mr. Lutz, Dr. Martin, Ms. Phillipps, Mr. Teirlinck and Mr. Vinnakota are independent. Mitchell P. Rales is the independent Chairman and a significant stockholder. The Board held 11 meetings during 2025.

The proxy discloses two related-person transactions involving Mr. Rales. The company rented a suite at Northwest Stadium, home of the Washington Commanders, in whose ownership group he is a member, for a $303,187.50 license fee for the 2025 - 2026 season. And he agreed to purchase $100.0 million of the Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock; he recused himself from the Board's vote, and an independent pricing committee approved the terms.

The preferred purchase shows the Chairman putting capital behind the company, but it also gives him a senior claim ahead of common holders. The process safeguards look appropriate.

idiosyncratic: Leverage and integration: the Eddyfi purchase raised debt at a time of lower margins. If integration disappoints, the balance sheet leaves little room for error.

Geopolitical disruption: the MD&A says the Middle East conflict, including logistics challenges from the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, decreased sales levels and increased inventory costs. The war in Ukraine adds further uncertainty.
Asbestos and legacy liabilities: the filing lists asbestos-related liabilities, insurance coverage litigation and the solvency of insurers among its risks.
Information gap: the share price has fallen far further than the filing alone would explain to us, which may reflect news or estimate changes we do not hold.
risks.systemic: The 10-K says demand for welding and cutting products depends largely on capital spending in manufacturing and industrial sectors, and that the industry has contracted during periods of slowing industrial activity. Tariffs on steel and aluminum and retaliatory trade measures add cost and demand risk; the MD&A says the IEEPA tariffs remain subject to ongoing litigation. Currency movements matter because most sales come from outside the United States.

body: BUY, target range $75–$95, on the scenario math in Valuation.

We would add conviction on evidence of debt reduction and margin recovery in the next two quarters. We would cut to HOLD if consensus estimates start falling, if Eddyfi integration slips, or if the cause of the share-price decline turns out to be a deterioration the filing does not yet show.
